summary:
Eric Bernhardson, Modal's CEO, introduces Modal as a fully managed infrastructure platform for data, AI, and machine learning workloads, designed to make writing these applications enjoyable again. With a background building Spotify's music recommendation system, Bernhardson started Modal during the pandemic to address poor developer experience in cloud computing. Modal targets 'high code' use cases where developers write custom code and models, positioning itself between Kubernetes and AWS Lambda—running arbitrary Python containers in a managed cloud with thousands of GPUs including H100s, A100s, L4s, and T4s.

The central insight driving Modal's architecture is that developer productivity depends on fast feedback loops. Cloud computing, while powerful, represented a step backward in developer experience. To achieve local-like iteration speed in the cloud, Modal abandoned Kubernetes and Docker entirely, building custom container systems, schedulers, and file systems—a multi-year effort still ongoing. Developers decorate Python functions with @app.function to create serverless functions. Live demonstrations show rapid container startup, H100 GPU access, in-code container image definition, fan-out of 10,000 invocations scaling to 18 containers, and persistent deployment endpoints.

Under the hood, Modal solves container cold start through several techniques. Container images are stored as metadata pointing to content-addressed blobs with checksum-based deduplication, exploiting redundancy across images. Lazy loading avoids pulling unneeded data. Python cold starts are particularly latency-sensitive due to sequential file accesses across thousands of modules, so Modal uses prefetching and task tracing based on historical access patterns. More recently, CPU memory snapshotting via gVisor dramatically cuts startup for large model workloads like Stable Diffusion (5-10 GB weights) to a couple of seconds. GPU snapshotting is being explored.

Modal uses gVisor for container isolation, Cloudflare R2 and CDN for storage across multiple regions, and solves a mixed integer programming problem to minimize total cost across cloud vendors. Serverless benefits include usage-based pricing, no capacity planning, and better GPU utilization through multi-tenant pooling. Modal offers $30/month in free credits and up to $50,000 for startups. Primary use cases include GenAI inference, batch jobs, computational biology, and LLM operations.

sections.title: Introduction and Modal Overview
sections.summary: Eric Bernhardson introduces himself as Modal's CEO, formerly at Spotify building music recommendation systems. Modal is a fully managed infrastructure platform for data/AI/ML, focusing on 'high code' use cases where developers write custom code and models. It positions itself like Kubernetes or AWS Lambda but fully managed and Python-native, running arbitrary containers with thousands of GPUs.

sections.title: Developer Experience and Custom Infrastructure
sections.summary: Bernhardson argues developer productivity depends on fast feedback loops, and cloud computing was a step backward for developer experience. To solve this, Modal had to build its own container system, scheduler, and file system from scratch, discarding Kubernetes and Docker. This is a deep rabbit hole and multi-year journey still ongoing.

sections.title: Modal Resources, Use Cases, and Customers
sections.summary: Modal provides access to thousands of GPUs (H100s, A100s, L4s, T4s) via Python SDK. Functions become serverless via decorators. Use cases include GenAI inference (diffusion models for music, video, images), batch jobs (medical imaging, computer vision), computational biology (protein folding), and LLM operations (fine-tuning, embeddings, inference). Customer Suno runs AI-generated music on Modal.

sections.title: Live Coding: Basic Function, GPU, and Custom Image
sections.summary: Live demo shows a basic square function with @app.function decorator executing in the cloud with streamed output and automatic code-change pickup. Then demonstrates running on an H100 by adding gpu='h100' to the decorator, defining a container image in code with pip_install('torch'), and verifying CUDA device name. Torch initialization adds about 1 second of overhead.

sections.title: Live Coding: Scaling, UI, and Deployment
sections.summary: Demo fans out 10,000 function invocations using map, scaling to 18 containers at peak. Modal UI shows container metrics, GPU temperature (33°C), and watt consumption. Deploying with modal deploy creates a persistent endpoint callable from any Python context; cold starts take a couple seconds, warm calls are faster, and containers stay warm for 60 seconds by default.

sections.title: Modal Under the Hood: Container Cold Start
sections.summary: Bernhardson explains Modal's custom infrastructure built on gVisor for isolation. Container images are stored as metadata pointing to content-addressed blobs with checksum-based deduplication, exploiting redundancy across images. Lazy loading avoids pulling unneeded data. Python cold starts are latency-sensitive due to sequential file accesses across thousands of modules; Modal uses prefetching and task tracing from historical runs. CPU memory snapshotting via gVisor dramatically cuts startup for large models like Stable Diffusion (5-10 GB weights) to a couple of seconds. GPU snapshotting is being explored. Storage uses Cloudflare R2 and CDN across multiple regions.

sections.title: Serverless Benefits and Capacity Management
sections.summary: Serverless enables paying only for used capacity, especially valuable for expensive GPUs. Pooling many users improves utilization, lowers cost, eliminates capacity planning, and reduces relative variance. Modal runs thousands of GPUs across multiple cloud vendors and regions, solving a mixed integer programming problem to minimize total cost. Customers can request 100 GPUs and get them instantaneously via maintained buffers.

sections.title: Why People Pick Modal and Getting Started
sections.summary: People pick Modal to run their own code with fast iteration, fully usage-based pricing, and no capacity planning. No need to build internal platforms or manage Kubernetes/Docker. Getting started is simple: pip install modal, with $30/month free credits for everyone and up to $50,000 in startup credits. Contact via erik@modal.com, Twitter @bernhardsson, or blog at bernhardsson.com.
